governance_boundary: This finite incidence package does not certify external support, consciousness, phenomenality, identity transfer, bridge-burden closure, or human mathematical review. It is an internal synthetic formal witness only.
independence_boundary: The package is constructed from a declared finite separator catalog, finite response-coordinate catalog, predeclared admission rules, and typed perturbation records. The construction does not assume separator atomicity; atomicity is only inferred later if the independently declared incidence graph passes the connectedness and completeness audit.
intended_theorem_use: If this finite package is accepted as separator-complete for the declared finite system model, graph connectedness implies separator atomicity relative to the finite factorization universe and therefore conditional closure of I_int.

finite_universe_policy.factor_nontriviality_rule: each factor side must contain at least one response-operative separator and at least one response coordinate
finite_universe_policy.zero_crossing_factor_locality_rule: a factor-local decomposition has no incidence edge crossing the cut
finite_universe_policy.anti_selection_rule: separator and response vertices must be admitted before connectivity and zero-crossing cut enumeration are inspected

separators.admission_rule: Admit before graph analysis if the test is expressible without referencing any proposed factor partition and can perturb a typed identity channel while preserving history typing.
Admit before graph analysis if the test is specified as a history-alignment perturbation with a fixed response coordinate and without using connectedness as a selection criterion.
Admit before graph analysis if the test modifies response phase under the fixed intervention grammar and is not chosen from a successful factor-cut search.
Admit before graph analysis if the test measures gauge stability under a predeclared perturbation family and does not presuppose separator atomicity.
Admit before graph analysis if the test is tied to intervention-fidelity loss under the frozen channel grammar and has a typed response coordinate.
Admit before graph analysis if the test probes factorization gap by a predeclared local-vs-global comparison without using the result of the zero-crossing cut audit.

responses.admission_rule: Admit if the coordinate is measurable from trace alignment records before graph connectivity is computed.
Admit if the coordinate is specified by intervention phase deltas before graph connectivity is computed.
Admit if the coordinate is generated by gauge response deltas before graph connectivity is computed.
Admit if the coordinate is a history-binding delta defined before graph connectivity is computed.
Admit if the coordinate is a factorization-probe delta defined before graph connectivity is computed and not selected to repair a disconnected graph.

perturbation_records.predeclared_measurement_rule: Record the signed delta on the stated response coordinate under a typed perturbation while preserving identity/history typing; admit the edge only if the delta margin is strictly positive before graph connectivity is inspected.
perturbation_records.note: Positive margin change under an admissible typed perturbation. This is synthetic internal evidence, not empirical data.

declared_limitations: Synthetic internal witness only; no human-subject data and no external campaign artifacts.
Completeness is finite and relative to the declared separator catalog and response-coordinate universe.
The package is not admissible as a witness if the separator catalog was chosen after inspecting graph connectedness or factor-local zero-crossing cuts.
A reviewer must verify that the catalog and perturbation records can be obtained operationally without presupposing atomicity before promoting this certificate.

declared_audit_metadata.interpretation_boundary: Metadata is derived from the finite declared graph only; it is not empirical support and not global separator completeness.
